title: S3 Bucket Policy
summary: An S3 bucket policy is a JSON resource-based policy attached directly to an object storage bucket that controls which principals may perform which actions against that bucket and the objects inside it, optionally under conditions. Because it is resource-based it can grant access to principals outside the owning account, which is what makes it the standard mechanism for cross-account sharing, public content delivery, and service integrations such as logging or content delivery networks. The policy is evaluated together with identity-based policies, access control lists, block-public-access settings, and any service control policies, and an explicit deny in any of those layers prevents the action. The most consequential failure modes are well known: a wildcard principal combined with a wildcard action, a listing permission that reveals object names, a condition intended to restrict access that does not actually match the request shape, and an object that was public before public access blocks were enabled. Security teams monitor bucket policy changes as high severity events because a single edit can expose an entire dataset, and they combine policy review with classification of what the bucket holds, encryption requirements, versioning, logging and lifecycle rules. Effective practice is to prefer identity-based access and role assumption over cross-account wildcards, to enforce encryption and TLS in the policy itself, and to keep public access blocks on unless a documented exception exists.
objectives: You will be able to read a bucket policy and determine whether it permits public or cross-account access.
You will be able to explain how bucket policies interact with identity policies, ACLs and public access blocks during authorisation.
You will be able to write conditions that restrict access by encryption, transport, network origin or principal tags.
You will be able to identify policy patterns that expose object listings or allow unintended read and write access.
You will be able to triage alerts raised by bucket policy changes and public access block modifications.
